scope: Fresh review of photo retry, maintained hidden readers, rapid navigation/rotation, mixed source aliases and resource release
test_changes: Added test/review/photo_retry_resume_review_test.dart with five independent combined/lifecycle cases

findings.title: Initial loading still starts for new photo widgets on a maintained hidden reader
findings.cause: The rasterizer and preparation/recovery continuations are guarded, but a single direct URL still builds CachedNetworkImage without checking activity. A newly mounted storage recovery state also calls _resolveSource from initState before its build visibility guard. The live cover/spread is a separate path from rasterized page preparation.
findings.trigger: A reader is kept underneath an opaque route and updated album data introduces a new cover photo while it is hidden; rotation was included in the actual reader reproduction. A newly mounted storage photo under TickerMode(false) similarly starts signing immediately.

tests: review: hidden reader rotation with a refreshed photo defers live-image work
review: a storage photo mounted while hidden must defer its initial signing request
proof.actual_reader_route: Real AlbumReaderSinglePageView under another Navigator route, verified TickerMode false

findings.recommendation: Apply activity gating before initial provider creation and storage resolution for every source branch, including the direct URL/live-cover path. Resume unresolved work on route/foreground visibility without adding parked contexts, unbounded listeners or polling timers.
findings.limits: The actual reader fixture verifies cache-manager image loading and real decoding. It does not prove that a warm production disk cache issues a new HTTP transfer; the confirmed problem is unnecessary hidden loading/decoding/signing work, not a demonstrated permanent memory leak.

findings.title: A direct URL and storage URI for the same failed image can still duplicate its download
findings.cause: Failure versions are keyed by logical source plus resolved URL, while the underlying image provider key uses the resolved URL/decode options. When a shared stream was created by the direct URL alias, its early observer records only that alias. A storage consumer cannot see the same rejected stream version and may reload it before its own error-widget recovery runs.
findings.trigger: Visible consumers and preparation use a direct URL and a supabase URI that resolve to the same image, with the same cache manager and 128x128 decode bounds; that URL is immediately rejected.

proof.test: review: URL and storage aliases of one rejected photo must share recovery

findings.recommendation: Associate shared failure/recovery identity with the effective image key so aliases of the same image observe the same failed generation, while keeping unrelated resource/cache/auth scopes isolated. Preserve the existing decode bounds, explicit retry semantics and bounded metadata lifetime.

verified_without_new_findings: All existing 220 related cases pass, including main/collection navigation, cover and reader rotation, page-turn cancel/reverse, photo recovery, hidden preparation, cache bounds, editor crop and print resolution
Eight rapid retry clicks, hiding during signing, changing decode size as on rotation, joining reader preparation and four further hide/resume cycles share one successful recovery
The combined retry/rotation case signs exactly three times (initial, automatic renewal, explicit retry) and downloads each resulting URL once
All image handles tracked in the combined case are disposed after unmount/cache clearing; live/pending image entries and transient callbacks return to zero
An actual maintained reader rotated without album data changes starts no additional photo loading in the new route test
The new findings do not reproduce a persistent missing-photo state or an unbounded/native memory leak

fresh_cases.note: The three new failures intentionally assert the desired behavior on the two unfixed findings

limits: Review only: production fixes are not included. Controlled signing/download fixtures use actual Flutter image decoding; the five new cases do not make live service calls. Existing cache-manager transport tests are included in the related suite. Cache/handle assertions do not measure whole-device memory or frame times and cannot establish the absence of every native leak or frame drop.
